H1.text: Two roads climb the same hill. Road one rises three metres for every ten metres you ride forward.

H2.text: Road two rises one metre for every two metres forward. Which road is steeper?

H3.text: Aarav has to pick one on his bicycle, on the way to college.

H4.text: Just looking is not enough. He needs one number that decides.

H5.text: That one number is called the slope. Let us find it.

I1.text: Think of a ramp. As you move along it, you go across, and you go up.

I2.text: The distance across is called the run. The height you gain is called the rise.

I3.text: Slope is rise divided by run: how much you go up for every one step across.

I4.text: Road one. Three divided by ten is zero point three.

I5.text: Road two. One divided by two is zero point five. Bigger slope, steeper road. Road two wins.

L1.text: Now let us put a line on graph paper, and turn it slowly.

L2.text: The angle the line makes with the x axis, measured anticlockwise, is called its inclination. We call it theta.

L3.text: At zero degrees the line is flat. It does not rise at all. Slope zero.

L4.text: As the line tips up, the slope grows. At forty five degrees, the rise equals the run. Slope one.

L5.text: Near ninety degrees the slope shoots up. Ten. Twenty. Over a hundred. At ninety, the line stands straight up.

L6.text: Now the run is zero, and we can never divide by zero. So the slope is not defined.

L7.text: Past ninety, the line falls as it goes right. Negative rise, so negative slope.

L8.text: In a right triangle, tan theta is the opposite side over the side next to theta. That is rise over run. So m equals tan theta.

D1.text: Now take two points on a line. P is x one, y one. Q is x two, y two.

D2.text: Step one. Draw a right triangle under the line, going across from P, then up to Q.

D3.text: Step two. The run is the change in x. That is x two minus x one.

D4.text: Step three. The rise is the change in y. That is y two minus y one.

D5.text: Step four. So m equals y two minus y one, over x two minus x one, when x one and x two are different.

K1.text: Side by side. This line goes up as you move right. Positive rise, positive slope. Theta is less than ninety.

K2.text: This line goes down as you move right. Negative rise, negative slope. Theta is more than ninety.

K3.text: Your turn. A line passes through two, five and six, one. Is its slope positive or negative? Pause and decide.

K4.text: Negative! As x grows from two to six, y drops from five to one. Rise minus four, run four. Slope minus one.

T1.text: Remember this. Slope is rise over run. Going up to the right means positive. Going down means negative.

V1.text: Two special lines. A flat line, like the x axis, has rise zero. So its slope is zero.

V2.text: A standing line, like the y axis, has run zero. So its slope is not defined.

V3.text: Quick one. A line passes through three, one and three, seven. What is its slope? Pause and think.

V4.text: Not defined! Both points have x equal to three. The line stands straight up, and the run is zero.

W2.text: Find the slope and the inclination of the line through minus one, two, and three, minus two.

W3.text: Step one. The rise. y two minus y one is minus two minus two. That is minus four.

W4.text: Step two. The run. x two minus x one is three minus minus one. That is four.

W5.text: Step three. The slope m is minus four over four. That is minus one.

W6.text: Step four. tan theta is minus one, so theta is more than ninety. Theta is one hundred and thirty five degrees.

X2.text: Slope through one, two and four, eight. Many students take y two minus y one on top, but x one minus x two below. Minus two.

X3.text: But the order must match, top and bottom. Six over three. The slope is plus two, and the line clearly goes up.

J1.text: Where is this asked? In JEE Main, for example in January twenty nineteen: find a missing coordinate from the slope through two points.

Q1.text: Exam level now. The line through A and B makes one hundred and thirty five degrees with the x axis. Find k. Pause and solve.

A1.text: The answer is B. Minus one.

A2.text: The slope is tan of one hundred and thirty five degrees, which is minus one.

A3.text: From the two points, the slope is two k minus three, over four minus k. Set that equal to minus one.

A4.text: So two k minus three equals k minus four, and k is minus one. Check: minus five over five is minus one.

F1.text: Here is your recap. Screenshot this card.

Y1.text: Can you answer these three questions without help?

Y2.text: One. What is the slope of a line that goes up three for every two across?

Y3.text: Two. Why is the slope of the y axis not defined?

Y4.text: Three. A line has inclination sixty degrees. What is its slope?

N1.text: Next time: two roads that never meet, and two that cross perfectly square. Their slopes hide a secret. Parallel and perpendicular lines.
